content.title: Post-Impact Combat Escalation | Substrate Damage, Recovery, Challenger Handoff
content.summary: A tunnel inspector recovers from a column impact before a grounded training duel. Preserve the five causal invariants and terminal proof while replacing every source-specific surface.

quick_start.input_format: A fixed substrate receives the first visible impact. + Damage remains after the subject recovers. + The challenger enters through established geography. + Every exchange has contact-bound displacement or residue. + The terminal pose retains both conflict and accumulated damage.
quick_start.recommended_input: Throw one adult tunnel inspector against a tiled pump-room column and release chips only from the contact zone. Bring one adult security trainer down the same marked aisle without changing geography. End on the inspector's stopped palm strike with the cracked column and both adult positions readable.
required_anchors: A fixed substrate receives the first visible impact.
Damage remains after the subject recovers.
Every exchange has contact-bound displacement or residue.
The terminal pose retains both conflict and accumulated damage.
usage_steps: Replace the example subject, setting, and surface details with an original concept.
Keep every required anchor and Creative DNA invariant causally visible.
Choose the MiniMax H3 or Seedance 2.0 prompt and fill only the declared variable slots.
Check duration, event order, camera continuity, sound, and anti-copy constraints before generation.
applicable_scope: A tunnel inspector recovers from a column impact before a grounded training duel. Preserve the five causal invariants and terminal proof while replacing every source-specific surface.
Original 4–15 second concepts that can preserve every required anchor.
MiniMax H3 or Seedance 2.0 projects that need a reusable causal video structure.
not_suitable_for: Requests that copy the source identity, setting, props, dialogue, or shot order.
Concepts that cannot show all required anchors inside the target duration.
Long-form exposition or unrelated multi-location stories without a compact causal chain.
